decision: Keep the source-lock completeness audit ACTIVE under its committed R3 output-path repair. R1 failed before reading source content; R2 successfully scanned the locked source inventory but could not write a ledger into the existing error-evidence directory. R3 repairs only that refusal while preserving the previous errors, source lock and audit scope. It remains the highest-value feasible local recovery because it can record the exact materialization boundary without changing any source or making an external request. Pipeline completeness remains broader but blocked on its independent checked-object receipt-semantics protocol gate.

categories.assessment: R3 retains the finite source-materialization ledger method after two narrow audit-tooling repairs. Pipeline completeness remains a broader but protocol-unready discovery method.
R1 and R2 preserve engineering failures, while R3 will create the reusable, hash-bound include-dependency ledger for the pinned source tree.

The repair and ledger remain entirely local and cannot support an upstream claim or external request. Pipeline completeness has no current external action but cannot be promoted until its local scientific gate is resolved.

R3 reuses only frozen source lock, pinned crate evidence and preserved controller errors; it does not fetch or substitute a byte. Pipeline completeness still needs a separately bound producer, adapter and receipt semantics before reuse is justified.
R3 directly removes the output-directory blocker while refusing to overwrite any ledger and retaining both prior incidents. Pipeline completeness remains blocked locally by its finite protocol gate.

candidates.rationale: ACTIVE under a committed R3 work record, output-path repair and exact R3 manifest. It runs only one static local ledger and preserves every prior tooling incident; no build, checker, network, retrieval, mutation or external action is in scope.

This remains the stronger broader conformance alternative, but no finite producer, adapter, checked-object receipt semantics, independently expected contents or fault rubric has been bound for execution.

blockers.reason: Bind the supported producer and adapters, a twelve-declaration expectation, receipt semantics, fixed faults and finite source/setup/build/tooling/process controls before promotion.
